newsitem.title: USA: Roslyn Bancorp soars in first trading.
newsitem.headline: Roslyn Bancorp soars in first trading.

text.p: Shares of Roslyn Bancorp, a Roslyn, N.Y., thrift which converted from mutual ownership into a stock company, soared on their first day of trading.
Sandler O'Neill & Partners LP, which managed the deal, said the issue of 42,371,359 shares was priced at $10 per share.
In the first day of trading the shares soared five to 15, equal to a 50 percent gain. Volume in mid-afternoon was 11.7 million shares.
A Wall Street trader, who did not want to be identified, said the shares were trading in excess of their value.
He said after the conversion the bank has excess equity. He noted that Roslyn has about $1.7 billion in assets and 42 million shares.
Officials of Roslyn could not be reached.
